references.text: Matthew's parallel account where Jesus sees the crowd and gives orders to cross to the other side of the sea.
Matthew's full parallel account of the storm on the sea, where Jesus gets into the boat with the disciples and calms the storm.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus says to the disciples, 'Let us go over to the other side,' and they take him in the boat.
Mark's full parallel account of the storm on the Sea of Galilee, which provides more details about the event.
The continuation of the journey in Luke's Gospel, where they arrive at the land of the Gerasenes on the other side of the sea.
Another event where Jesus crosses the Sea of Galilee (Sea of Tiberias) with his disciples, showing a similar pattern of crossing over.
The psalm describes those who go out to sea, experience a storm, cry out to the Lord in their distress, and he calms the storm—a Old Testament foreshadowing of Jesus' power over natural forces.
Jonah's story about the storm at sea where the prophet slept while the disciples/sailors were afraid has clear parallels to Jesus sleeping during the storm on the sea.
